messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 3-chloropyridine with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:
ligand:
L1: tBuBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L2: tBuXPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C=CC=C2]
L3: XPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C=CC=C2]
L4: AdBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P([C@@]3(C[C@@H]4C5)C[C@H](C4)C[C@H]5C3)[C@]6(C7)C[C@@H](C[C@@H]7C8)C[C@@H]8C6)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

base:
B1: BTMG [SMILES CC(C)(C)/N=C(N(C)C)/N(C)C]
B2: P2Et [SMILES CN(C)P(N(C)C)(N(C)C)=NP(N(C)C)(N(C)C)=NCC]
B3: MTBD [SMILES CN1CCCN2C1=NCCC2]

additive:
A1: 5-phenylisoxazole [SMILES C1(C2=CC=CC=C2)=CC=NO1]
A2: 4-phenylisoxazole [SMILES C1(C2=CC=CC=C2)=CON=C1]
A3: 3-phenylisoxazole [SMILES C1(C2=CC=CC=C2)=NOC=C1]
A4: 5-(dibenzylamino)isoxazole [SMILES C1(N(CC2=CC=CC=C2)CC3=CC=CC=C3)=CC=NO1]
A5: 3-(dibenzylamino)isoxazole [SMILES C1(N(CC2=CC=CC=C2)CC3=CC=CC=C3)=NOC=C1]
A6: 1,2-benzisoxazole [SMILES C12=C(C=CC=C2)ON=C1]
A7: 2,1-benzisoxazole [SMILES C12=CON=C1C=CC=C2]
A8: ethyl 5-methylisoxazole-4-carboxylate [SMILES CC1=C(C(OCC)=O)C=NO1]
A9: ethyl 5-methylisoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES CC1=CC(C(OCC)=O)=NO1]
A10: 3,5-dimethylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=CC(C)=NO1]
A11: 5-methyl-3-(pyrrol-1-yl)isoxazole [SMILES CC1=CC(N2C=CC=C2)=NO1]
A12: 5-methylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=CC=NO1]
A13: ethyl 3-methylisoxazole-5-carboxylate [SMILES CC1=NOC(C(OCC)=O)=C1]
A14: 3-methyl-5-phenylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=NOC(C2=CC=CC=C2)=C1]
A15: 3-methylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=NOC=C1]
A16: ethyl isoxazole-4-carboxylate [SMILES CCOC(C1=CON=C1)=O]
A17: ethyl isoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES CCOC(C1=NOC=C1)=O]
A18: ethyl 3-methoxyisoxazole-5-carboxylate [SMILES COC1=NOC(C(OCC)=O)=C1]
A19: 5-(2,6-difluorophenyl)isoxazole [SMILES FC(C=CC=C1F)=C1C2=CC=NO2]
A20: methyl isoxazole-5-carboxylate [SMILES O=C(OC)C1=CC=NO1]
A21: methyl 5-(furan-2-yl)isoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES O=C(OC)C1=NOC(C2=CC=CO2)=C1]
A22: methyl 5-(thiophen-2-yl)isoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES O=C(OC)C1=NOC(C2=CC=CS2)=C1]

Experiments so far (best first):
L2 | B2 | A14 -> 52.0%
L1 | B1 | A5 -> 32.7%
L4 | B3 | A12 -> 11.3%
L1 | B3 | A18 -> 2.4%
L1 | B2 | A17 -> 0.0%

Propose exactly 20 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"ligand": "<label>", "base": "<label>", "additive": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: This tests whether the strong A14 result depends on its 3-methyl substituent while retaining the 5-phenyl group and best observed catalyst/base pair.
This probes whether changing the phenylisoxazole substitution pattern from A14 improves the additive effect under the best observed catalyst/base pair.
This tests the phenyl regioisomer of A14 to assess how isoxazole substitution position affects the high-yielding condition.
This evaluates a close 5-arylisoxazole analogue of A14 with electron-withdrawing aryl fluorines.
This tests whether a simple methylisoxazole retains useful additive activity without A14's phenyl group.
This compares the complementary methylisoxazole substitution pattern with the successful A14 additive.
This checks whether adding a second methyl group to a small isoxazole additive improves performance.
This tests a dibenzylamino-substituted analogue to assess whether a more electron-rich, bulky isoxazole additive helps.
This retests the dibenzylamino isoxazole under the best observed ligand/base pair, separating additive effects from the earlier weaker conditions.
This evaluates a methylated ester-substituted isoxazole as a structurally distinct additive under the best observed conditions.
This compares an ester-bearing isoxazole regioisomer to determine whether its substitution pattern affects yield.
This tests an alternate methyl/ester substitution pattern while retaining the successful catalyst/base pair.
This assesses a compact ester-substituted isoxazole additive without the extra methyl or aryl groups.
This probes a heteroaryl-substituted ester isoxazole for potential additive effects distinct from A14.
This tests the thiophene analogue of A21 to compare heteroaryl identity under the best observed conditions.
This isolates the ligand change from the best observed condition and tests whether tBuBrettPhos can outperform tBuXPhos with A14.
This tests the XPhos scaffold against the top observed ligand/base/additive combination while changing only the ligand.
This evaluates AdBrettPhos with the best observed base and additive, separating its effect from the earlier low-yielding condition.
This tests BTMG with the top ligand and additive to isolate whether the base contributed to the best observed yield.
This tests MTBD with the top ligand and additive to directly compare bases without the earlier confounding changes.
